subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Please don’t confuse me __by giving so man__y different directions.
solution:
The correct answer is "**no substitution required**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**By giving so many**" is grammatically **correct**.
 
• The **preposition** **"by"** is used to show **how work is done**.
 
 
• **Example:*** Mike travels **by** bus. *
 
 
 
• The **verb "giving**" is in the correct form of a tense, which is **present continuous** because the action is going on. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Sera is **giving** massages at a nearby parlour.* 
 
 
 
• The **phrase "so many"** denotes the **unspecific quantity**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Martha has **so many** works left undone. *
 
 
 
• As the phrase "by giving so many" justifies its usage, no substitution is required. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **sentence** must justify the **subject-verb concord** to be grammatically correct. 
 
• **The subject** is the **noun or pronoun** about which the sentence is. 
 
• Subject-verb concord means the **subject and verb must agree in number.**
 
• If the **subject is singular**, the **verb** should also be **singular** and if the **subject** is **plural**, the **verb** must also be **plural**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *The **boys want** to play cricket but **she wants** to play basketball. *
